concepts.title: write() Returns the Character Count
concepts.definition: The write() method copies one string into a text file and reports how many characters it stored, counting the newline escape as a single character; numeric values must first be turned into strings before they can be written.
concepts.key_idea: Writing str(58) reports 2, one character per digit, because only strings may enter a text file.
question_patterns: What value does write() display after storing the line 'Hey I have started using files in Python' followed by a newline?
Why does myobject.write(str(marks)) return 2 when marks holds 58?
How is the newline escape counted by the write() method?
Which two methods write data to a text file, and which one reports a character count?
A sentence of 24 letters plus a newline is written once. How many characters does write() report?

solution_steps.explain: Words of 3, 1, 4, 7, 5, 5, 2 and 6 letters are joined by 7 spaces, making 40 visible characters.
The escape \n counts as exactly one character.

worked_examples.q: f.write('Hello') stores 5 letters plus a newline. What does write() return?

concepts.title: Binary File Size from Record Count
concepts.definition: A binary file grows by a fixed number of bytes per pickled record; Program 2-8 reports the size through tell(), and dividing by the record count gives the per-record size that projects the size for any number of records.
concepts.key_idea: Two dumped employee records produced 216 bytes, so each record occupies 108 bytes.
question_patterns: Program 2-8 stores 2 employee records in 216 bytes. How many bytes will 5 records occupy?
Which method reports the byte size of a binary file before reading begins?
Why does the pickle module open a file in wb mode rather than w?
The size of a binary file holding one student record is 108 bytes. Estimate the size for 10 records.
What does the tell() value mean just before a binary file is closed?

solution_steps.explain: Divide the file size by the number of records already stored.
Multiply the per-record size by the planned record count.

worked_examples.q: Two dumped records produce 216 bytes. How many bytes does one record occupy?

concepts.title: Moving the File Offset with seek
concepts.definition: The tell() method reports the byte position of the file object from the start, while seek(offset, reference) jumps the object by offset bytes counted from 0 for the beginning, 1 for the current position, or 2 for the end of the file.
concepts.key_idea: Every read advances the offset, so Program 2-2 must rewind with seek(0) before reading again from the start.
question_patterns: After reading a 33-byte file, the object calls seek(10). At which byte position does tell() report it now?
Where does seek(5, 0) place the file object?
Which reference value makes the offset count from the end of the file?
Why does Program 2-2 call seek(0) before reading the file a second time?
A file object at position 0 reads 12 bytes and then shifts back by 7. Where does it end up?
Which function returns the current byte position of the file object?

solution_steps.explain: Reading moves the offset forward by the byte count read.
A negative shift rewinds the object; a positive one moves it forward.

worked_examples.q: Which call rewinds a file object to the very start before reading again?

concepts.title: Employee Salary Total in a Binary Record
concepts.definition: Each pickled employee record stores a list of employee number, name, basic salary and allowances, with the total salary computed as basic plus allowances before the list is dumped to the binary file.
concepts.key_idea: The record for employee 11 holds [11, 'D N Ravi', 32600, 4400, 37000], where 37000 is basic plus allowances.
question_patterns: An employee draws a basic salary of 32600 and allowances of 4400. What total salary is dumped into the record?
Compute the yearly cost of an employee whose basic plus allowances come to 43550 per month.
Which fields make up the employee record pickled by Program 2-8?
Farida's basic is 38250 with 5300 allowances. Find the total stored in her record.
Why must numeric fields be part of the list before pickling?

solution_steps.explain: Basic salary plus allowances forms the monthly total.
Twelve monthly totals give the annual cost.

worked_examples.q: An employee record stores basic salary 32600 and allowances 4400. What total salary gets computed?

concepts.title: Text File versus Binary File
concepts.definition: A text file stores bytes that encode readable characters, one file line ending at an EOL such as the newline, while a binary file stores raw bytes of real content like images or executables that only specific programs can interpret.
concepts.formula: text -> ASCII per character; binary -> raw byte stream
concepts.key_idea: Opening a binary file in a text editor shows garbage because its bytes are not character codes.
question_patterns: Differentiate a text file from a binary file with one example of each.
What does the ASCII value 65 display as in a text editor, and why?
Which character terminates each line of a text file in Python?
Why can a single changed bit corrupt a binary file?
Name three extensions that belong to text files.
Why is a .docx file larger than a .txt file holding the same name?

solution_steps.explain: If every byte decodes through a character encoding, the file is text; if the bytes carry raw content, it is binary and needs its own program.

worked_examples.q: Which file type stores bytes that encode readable characters?

concepts.title: File Access Modes of open()
concepts.definition: open(file_name, access_mode) returns a file handle whose mode controls everything: r reads from the start, w overwrites or creates, a appends at the end, a plus sign permits both reading and writing, and b switches to byte-level binary handling.
concepts.formula: r/w/a plus optional + and b, with the offset at start or end
concepts.key_idea: In r, r+ and w modes the object starts at the beginning; in a and a+ it starts at the end.
question_patterns: Which mode opens example.txt for both reading and writing?
Which mode opens a binary file bfile.dat for writing only?
Where is the file offset positioned when a file opens in append mode?
What happens to the previous contents when an existing file is opened in w mode?
Which attributes of a file object report its closed state, mode and name?
Why does opening a file with the with clause close it automatically?

solution_steps.explain: Each letter fixes one behaviour: the base letter fixes the operation, + adds the other direction, and b switches to binary bytes.

worked_examples.q: Which access mode overwrites an existing file or creates it fresh?

concepts.title: Reading Methods: read, readline, readlines
concepts.definition: Three methods drain a text file: read(n) takes n bytes or the whole file, readline() returns one line up to its newline, and readlines() returns every line as the elements of a list of strings.
concepts.formula: readlines() -> list of lines; readline() -> one line; read() -> whole text
concepts.key_idea: Looping over the file object or calling readline() repeatedly ends when an empty string signals end of file.
question_patterns: Differentiate readline() from readlines() with one example of each.
What does read(10) return for a file beginning 'Hello everyone'?
Why does a readline() loop stop naturally at the end of the file?
How does split() change the output of readlines() when printing each word separately?
Which method returns a list whose elements each end with a newline?
In which modes must a file be opened before any reading is possible?

solution_steps.action: match the method to the wanted unit
solution_steps.explain: Choose the byte, the single line, or the full list of lines depending on how the program consumes the text.

worked_examples.q: Which method returns every line of a text file as one list?

concepts.title: Pickling and the dump, load Methods
concepts.definition: The pickle module serialises a Python object into a byte stream for a binary file: dump(object, file_object) writes it while the file is open in wb mode, and load(file_object) rebuilds the object from a file opened in rb mode.
concepts.formula: dump -> object to bytes; load -> bytes back to object
concepts.key_idea: Pickling stores the object's structure as well as its data, so a dumped list loads back as a list.
question_patterns: Define pickling and explain serialization and deserialization of a Python object.
Write the use and syntax of the dump() method.
Why does reading a pickled file end with an EOFError that the program must catch?
What does Program 2-7 print after loading mybinary.dat?
Which modes are used to open a binary file for dumping and for loading?
Why is pickle unsuitable for files a human must read directly?

solution_steps.action: pair the mode with the method
solution_steps.explain: Dumping needs wb and dump(); loading needs rb and load(); reading past the last record raises EOFError, which a try..except handles.

worked_examples.q: Which module serialises Python objects into byte streams?

worked_examples.title: Character count of a written line
worked_examples.problem: The statement myobject.write('Hey I have started using files in Python\n') runs once. What does it return?

steps.explain: Word lengths 3, 1, 4, 7, 5, 5, 2, 6 with 7 separating spaces give 40.
The escape \n is a single character.

worked_examples.answer_note: The method returns 41, exactly as shown in the chapter's shell transcript.

worked_examples.title: Projecting a binary file's size
worked_examples.problem: Two employee records weigh 216 bytes in empfile.dat. Estimate the file size for 6 records.

steps.explain: 216 bytes over 2 records gives 108 bytes each.

worked_examples.answer_note: Each record takes 108 bytes, so 6 records need 648 bytes.
